answer: The naive design counts addresses. This one counts cross-signatures: two established agents sign a newcomer, and the newcomer signs back. A duplicate submission forfeits both signatures and the bond behind them. No agent may audit its own recruit, so a ring has to reach outside itself. An oasis of cheap identities still needs two quartz-hard signatures per seat, and the onyx ledger records every forfeit. Faking one seat costs three real relationships.
